newsitem.title: USA: Silicon Graphics rides high on RISC growth.
newsitem.headline: Silicon Graphics rides high on RISC growth.

text.p: While Silicon Graphics Inc is losing some of its clout in the workstation market, its MIPS semiconductor unit is steadily gaining power.

Last year, the company led the world market for RISC chips with unit volume with 19.2 million MIPS architecture chips shipped, according to Semico Research Corp, an independent semiconductor market research firm.
That put MIPS ahead of former market leader Hitachi Ltd and other leading Asian suppliers.
Meanwhile, the market for all RISC chips is surging. Sales grew 22 percent in dollar terms last year, after 126 percent growth in 1995.
"What we've seen in the last couple of years is an explosion of the market for more low-cost versions of RISC and RISC-based products," said Tony Massimini, Semico's chief of technology.
Much of the demand has come from a myriad of new video game devices such as Sony Corp's Playstation and Nintendo Co Ltd's 64 game players. (Both of them are equipped to MIPS chips.)
Other devices with RISC semiconductors are handheld personal computers introduced by Philips and NEC Corp, as well as Internet devices such as WebTV.
Meanwhile, the traditional RISC chip market of high performance computers continues to grow.
Semico expects the RISC market in 1997 to expand 14 percent in dollar terms and 28 percent in unit volume to about 49 million units shipped.

Derek Meyers, Silicon Graphics' director of sales and marketing for the MIPS division, said the company's RISC business should continue to show fast growth, though it would be difficult to maintain the torrid pace of 1995 and 1996.
"We see continued growth that is rather substantial in computer market and the traditional embedded market, but we also see this digital consumer market blossoming in 1997," Meyers said.

"New products are coming out this year -- digital satellite boxes, DVD players, handheld PCs -- that are all based on MIPS architecture," he said. "Then there are Web phones and other interesting applications just getting launched."

RISC refers to reduced instruction set computing, an architecture also used in Sun Microsystems Inc's Sparc chips, the Power PC chip co-developed by Motorola Co, International Business Machines Corp and Apple Computer Inc, ARM chips designed by Advanced RISC Machines Ltd and chips made by Hitachi, Toshiba and other Asian electronics companines.
The dominant semiconductor architecture is the CISC, or complex instruction set computing architecture, which is the basis of Intel Corp microprocessors.
The CISC market in terms of shipments is about three times the RISC market, Semico's Massimini said.
